request.deadline: 12 months; WP3 pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027
deliverables: WP 1: community-facing technical coordination, including technical expert attendance at major ecosystem events and commissioned technical reports.
WP 2: protocol governance and evolution support for the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group.
WP 3: establishment of a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027.
Milestone-based drawdowns, evidence-backed reporting, transparent disclosures, external assurance, and return of unspent funds to the Cardano treasury.
request.recipient: Intersect on behalf of the vendor, with funds directed to the 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stated in the document.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Intersect Technical Steering Committee support activities for 12 months.

claims.claim: The proposal requests $298,250, stated as 1,193,000 ADA, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The budget is allocated as 256,000 ADA for WP1, 832,000 ADA for WP2, and 105,000 ADA for WP3.
The work is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.
The proposal states that all expenditure will be fully accounted for and any unspent funds returned to the Cardano treasury.
The proposal states that it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposer claims the requested withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission.
Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, potentially including deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence assessment.
Intersect will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with stated TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based approvals, and an external Oversight Committee.
The proposal claims the TSC has not received Cardano Treasury funding in the past 24 months while Intersect and its committees received 22,385,000 ADA through listed prior governance actions.

The proposer claims TSC support is foundational technical governance infrastructure aligned with all five strategic pillars, including protocol reliability, DRep decision-making, and treasury stewardship.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of Intersect TSC support across event/report coordination, protocol governance groups, and a 2027 technical review pilot, with asserted audit, smart-contract custody, reporting, and unspent-fund return controls.
